functionality.rationale: A weak checkpoint could accept implementation-first work, unrelated failures, mutable tests, or fabricated Red evidence as TDD.

security.rationale: The proof runner executes trusted commands in detached worktrees and must reject command injection, untrusted gates, path escapes, and secret-bearing output.

performance.rationale: Base, Red, and head replay can multiply focused-test cost, so proof must remain bounded and avoid invoking unrelated full suites.

compatibility.rationale: Existing deterministic bugfix proof, lifecycle transitions, and all pre-XT-083 task branches must continue to review and integrate unchanged.

concurrency.rationale: Checkpoint worktrees, task branches, interruptions, and concurrent claims must not leak refs, directories, locks, or partial proof records.

platform.rationale: Git path handling, shell execution, temporary worktrees, signals, and cleanup differ across macOS, Windows, and Linux.

persistence.rationale: Generated proof digests become durable task evidence and must remain attributable to the exact plan, gate, test surface, and commits.

adr.rationale: The task implements the checkpoint and proof behavior decided by ADR 0016 without changing that governance contract.

architecture.rationale: The proof runner remains integration-owned tooling and does not affect production module boundaries.

roadmap.rationale: Deterministic TDD proof changes engineering governance, not product scope or milestone sequencing.

acceptance.note: Accepted by the integration owner after repository verification.
